Mechanically damage isolated myofibers in a culture dish using a Pasteur pipette.
Confirm myofiber damage by visual inspection for shrunken morphology.
Co-culture intact myofibers with damaged myofibers in a culture dish.
Perform immunofluorescence analysis of MYOD and satellite cells on intact myofibers co-cultured with damaged myofibers using a fluorescence microscope.
Wash out damaged myofibers and culture media containing DMDFs in the culture dish and replace with fresh DMEM for 24 h.

sentences: Cut formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded lung tissues into 4-µm-thick sections using a microtome.
Boil lung tissue sections in 10-mM sodium carbonate buffer for 20 minutes.
Permeabilize boiled lung tissue sections with PBS 0.5% Triton X-100.
Incubate permeabilized lung tissue sections with blocking buffer for 1 hour at room temperature.
Stain blocked lung tissue sections with rabbit anti-human citrullinated histone H3 antibody at 1:100 and goat anti-human myeloperoxidase (MPO) antibody at 1:40 for 1 hour at room temperature.
Add donkey anti-rabbit IgG Alexa Fluor 568 and donkey anti-goat IgG Alexa Fluor 488 secondary antibodies at 1:200 to stained lung tissue sections for 2 hours at room temperature in the dark.
Counterstain lung tissue sections with secondary antibodies using DAPI at 1:1000 for 2 hours at room temperature in the dark.
Mount stained and counterstained lung tissue sections on glass slides with 10 µl ProLong Antifade reagent.
Store mounted lung tissue sections in the dark overnight at room temperature.
Analyze stored lung tissue sections using a fluorescence microscope with standard filter sets.
Quantify NET volume in lung tissue sections using Imaris software with three-dimensional reconstruction.
Scan entire lung tissue sections using the Nanozoomer 2.0-HT system and manually screen for NET-rich areas.

sentences: Seed 1.5e6 Cor3-1 cells in a 10 cm dish for cellular fractionation.
Seed 1.0e6 P19 cells in a 10 cm dish for cellular fractionation.
Transfect P19 cells with 3 μg Ascl1 plasmid constructs for subsequent protein isolation from chromatin fractions.
Wash cells once with room temperature PBS.
Scrape cells into 1 ml PBS.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 1200 rpm and 4°C for 3 minutes to pellet cells.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 5 volumes of ice-cold E1 buffer and gently pipette up and down 5 times.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 3400 rpm and 4°C for 2 minutes to separate the supernatant as the cytoplasmic fraction.
Collect the cytoplasmic fraction supernatant into a fresh tube.
Resuspend the pellet in E1 buffer and gently pipette.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 3400 rpm and 4°C for 2 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in ice-cold E2 buffer and gently pipette in the same volume used for E1 buffer.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 3400 rpm and 4°C for 2 minutes.
Collect the nucleus fraction supernatant into a fresh tube.
Resuspend the pellet in ice-cold E3 buffer and gently pipette in the same volume used for E1.
Sonicate the chromatin fraction using a Bioruptor with settings H, 30 sec ON/30 sec OFF for 5 minutes.
Centrifuge the sonicated chromatin fraction at 13000 rpm and 4°C for 10 minutes.
Determine the protein concentration of the chromatin fraction using a BCA protein assay kit.

sentences: Sacrifice the DSS-treated mice using the CO2 chamber.
Collect a 50 mg piece of proximal colon from the sacrificed mice using a scalpel and forceps and weigh it on the weighing scale.
Isolate total RNA from the collected colonic tissues using TRIzol reagent according to the manufacturer's protocol.
Incubate the RNA sample with 0.1 volume of 8 M LiCl diluted in RNase-free water on ice for 2 hours.
Centrifuge the RNA-LiCl mixture at 14,000 g for 30 minutes at 4°C using a centrifuge.
Pour out the supernatant from the centrifuge tube, leaving the RNA pellet in the tube.
Dissolve the RNA pellet in 200 μl of RNase-free water.
Repeat the incubation of the RNA solution with 0.1 volume of 8 M LiCl diluted in RNase-free water on ice for 2 hours.
Repeat the centrifugation of the RNA-LiCl mixture at 14,000 g for 30 minutes at 4°C using a centrifuge.
Pour out the supernatant from the centrifuge tube, leaving the RNA pellet in the tube.
Dissolve the RNA pellet in 200 μl of RNase-free water.
Precipitate the RNA at −20°C for 30 minutes in 0.1 volume of 3 M sodium acetate (pH 5.2) and 2 volumes of 100% absolute ethanol.
Centrifuge the RNA-ethanol mixture at 14,000 g for 30 minutes at 4°C using a centrifuge.
Wash the RNA pellet with 100 μl of 70% ethanol and centrifuge at 14,000 g for 10 minutes at 4°C using a centrifuge.
Remove the supernatant from the centrifuge tube after the ethanol wash.
Dissolve the RNA pellet in 20-50 μl of RNase-free water.
Assess the integrity of the purified RNA using 2% agarose gel electrophoresis with electrophoresis equipment.

sentences: Split confluent plates of 293T cells 1:4 in culture medium to ensure optimal cell density for transfection the next day.
Transfect each plate of 293T cells with 1 μg gag/pol construct, 1.5 μg enhanced GFP reporter construct, and 1.5 μg envelope-expressing construct using Fugene-6 transfection reagent.
Collect the supernatant from the transfected 293T cells at 48 h and 72 h post-transfection.
Filter the collected supernatant through 0.45-μm filters.
Store the filtered supernatant at –80°C.
Infect 293T, TE671, and QT6/ACE2 cells with the viral vector.
Determine eGFP titers 72 h after infection by fluorescence-activated cell sorter (FACS).
Heat inactivate patient serum samples at 56°C for 30 min.
Serially dilute the heat-inactivated serum samples from 1:10 in culture medium by 2-fold.
Mix the 2-fold serially diluted serum samples with MLV(SARS) virions at a 1:1 vol/vol ratio.
Incubate the serum-virion mixture at 37°C for 1 h.
Add 100 μL of the serum-virus mixture to QT6/ACE2 cells seeded at 1 × 10^4 cells per well in 96-well flat-bottomed tissue culture plates.
Count GFP-positive cells 48 h later by fluorescence microscopy.

sentences: Sow Phaseolus vulgaris genotypes seeds in vermiculite.
Place seed-containing vermiculite in a growth chamber set to 23°C with a 16 h light/8 h dark cycle and 75% relative humidity.
Cultivate seedlings in plastic pots filled with moist vermiculite for 10–12 days until primary leaves are fully-expanded.
Transplant three seedlings into a 20 cm plastic pot with moist vermiculite.
Place the plastic pot with seedlings in a dark room for 24 hours prior to inoculation.
Prepare a 20 μL DNA-plasmid mix of BPMV RNA1 and RNA2 plasmids in 50 mM potassium phosphate buffer, pH 7.0, using a pipette.
Grind the infected leaf of P. vulgaris cv. Black Valentine in a mortar with mock buffer to make leaf sap.
Mechanically rub one primary leaf with the DNA-plasmid mix or leaf sap using a gloved hand.
Allow the inoculated plants to grow at 19°C under a 16 h light/8 h dark cycle in a growth chamber.
